display.purpose: Measured values only — freshness %, critical count, days remaining, streak days.

body.purpose: Descriptions, recipe steps, chat, explanatory copy.

label.purpose: Uppercase engraved panel markings and status chips. Always >=600 weight with >=0.1em tracking.

shadows.name: neu-raised
shadows.purpose: Default resting state for cards, tiles and panels.

shadows.name: neu-raised-sm
shadows.purpose: Compact controls where full distance looks inflated.

shadows.name: neu-inset
shadows.purpose: Inputs, and any selected option. A groove in the panel.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Count-up tweens and bar fills; decelerates hard so the final value settles.

motion.name: spring-pill
motion.purpose: Shared-element layoutId pill sliding between tabs.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disables float, blob-drift, sheen and hover translate. Static neumorphic depth is retained — it is styling, not movement.

components.name: Pressable Tile
components.description: The default soft-UI control. Same colour as its ground; defined entirely by its shadow pair. Raises, lifts on hover, presses inward on click.
components.css: .ds-tile { display: block; text-align: left; width: 200px; background: var(--neu-surface, #e9ebf1); color: var(--foreground, #111111); border: none; border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; box-shadow: 6px 6px 14px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), -6px -6px 14px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); transition: box-shadow 240ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); cursor: pointer; } .ds-tile:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 8px 8px 18px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), -8px -8px 18px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); } .ds-tile:active { transform: translateY(0); box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), inset -4px -4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-tile-label { display: block; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; opacity: 0.55; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-tile-value { display: block; font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.1; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ink fill on the instrument body. One per region, for the single most likely action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #111111; color: #e9ebf1; border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 20px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Inset Input
components.description: A groove in the panel, never a raised block. The inset shadow does not change on focus; only a ring is added.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 260px; background: var(--neu-surface, #e9ebf1); color: var(--foreground, #111111); border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.04); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), inset -4px -4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); transition: border-color 300ms, box-shadow 300ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(17,17,17,0.35); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: rgba(17,17,17,0.35); box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), inset -4px -4px 9px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)), 0 0 0 2px rgba(17,17,17,0.12); }

components.name: Reading Chip
components.description: A read-only measurement. 10% wash, 20% border, solid text, all in one readout colour.
components.html: CRITICAL Matches Diet Allergens Unknown
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; } .ds-chip-danger { background: rgba(229,72,77,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(229,72,77,0.2); color: #e5484d; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-chip-safe { background: rgba(48,164,108,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(48,164,108,0.2); color: #30a46c; } .ds-chip-unknown { background: rgba(17,17,17,0.08); border: 1px solid transparent; color: rgba(17,17,17,0.5); }

components.css: .ds-card { width: 320px; background: var(--neu-surface, #e9ebf1); color: var(--foreground, #111111); border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; box-shadow: 6px 6px 14px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), -6px -6px 14px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); transition: box-shadow 240ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 8px 8px 18px var(--neu-shadow-dark, rgba(160,172,196,0.7)), -8px -8px 18px var(--neu-shadow-light, rgba(255,255,255,0.95)); } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 16px; } .ds-grade { width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 6px; background: #30a46c; color: #fff; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 900; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; flex: 1; } .ds-readout { border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06); border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px; } .ds-readout-label { display: block; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; opacity: 0.45; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-readout-row { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 8px; } .ds-readout-value { font-size: 30px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1; color: #e5484d; } .ds-readout-unit { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.6; } .ds-bar { flex: 1; height: 10px; border-radius: 999px; background: rgba(17,17,17,0.1); overflow: hidden; align-self: center; } .ds-bar-fill { display: block; width: 8%; height: 100%; border-radius: 999px; background: #e5484d; }

components.css: .ds-dialog { width: 300px; background: var(--card, #e9ebf1); color: var(--foreground, #111111); border: 1px solid var(--border, #d7dae3); border-radius: 24px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); } .ds-dialog-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, #d7dae3); } .ds-dialog-title { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-dialog-close { width: 32px; height: 32px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; background: rgba(17,17,17,0.1); color: inherit; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background 200ms; } .ds-dialog-close:hover { background: rgba(17,17,17,0.2); } .ds-dialog-body { padding: 16px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; opacity: 0.6; }

narrative.overview:
Nutri-Trust looks like a calibrated measuring device, not a lifestyle app. The body of the instrument is a single continuous neutral surface — every panel, tile, card and control is carved from the same sheet, and depth comes only from the way light falls across it. Nothing is tinted to attract attention. Nothing floats on a different-coloured plate.

Colour enters only where the instrument reports a reading. Green, amber and red are not brand colours; they are measurements of how close food is to being wasted. Because the rest of the interface is deliberately colourless, a single red badge is impossible to miss on a shelf of twenty items. This is the visual expression of the product's first principle: the name is trust, so the interface must never overstate what it knows. A surface that shouts everywhere can't be believed when it shouts about something real.

The material is soft-UI — surfaces raise, lift under a cursor, and physically press inward when clicked — but the tactility is disciplined rather than decorative. Motion follows the same rule: it exists to confirm a physical action or to make a number legible as it changes, and it stops entirely when the operating system asks it to.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous material; hierarchy from shadow, never from fill colour
A greyscale instrument body with a strict three-colour readout
Tactile controls that raise, lift, and press
Mobile-first single column, capped at a hand's width
Depth that survives both light and dark without changing its logic

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Colour is a measurement, not decoration. Green, amber and red state how close something is to being wasted or how risky it is to eat — nothing else, ever. If a colour on screen isn't reporting a reading, it is a bug.

rules.name: The One Material Rule
rules.body: --background, --card and --neu-surface are the same value and must stay that way. The moment a surface is tinted a different shade from the page, the soft-UI illusion collapses into 'a grey box on a lighter grey page.' Depth is shadow's job.

rules.name: The Earned Alarm Rule
rules.body: Because the body is colourless, red carries real weight. Never spend it on anything the user cannot act on.

rules.name: The Engraved Label Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase labels are always >=600 weight with >=0.1em tracking. Uppercase at small sizes without tracking is unreadable on a phone, and this system uses uppercase constantly.

rules.name: The Big Number Rule
rules.body: A measured value gets Display weight and negative tracking; its unit and caption stay Body or Label. The number is the reading; the words around it are the engraving.

rules.name: The Single Light Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the top-left, always. Every raised surface is dark-shadowed bottom-right and light-shadowed top-left. A shadow pair in any other direction breaks the whole panel's illusion, not just its own element.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Interactive surfaces must complete the physical loop: raised at rest, lifted on hover, inset on press. A soft-UI control that doesn't depress on click reads as a picture of a button rather than a button.

rules.name: The Matching Ground Rule
rules.body: Before applying any neu- class, confirm the element's parent background equals --neu-surface. On a different ground, override the scope's tokens (as .neu-scope-navy does) rather than accepting grey-on-colour mud.

dos: Do keep --background, --card and --neu-surface identical. Changing one without the others is the single fastest way to break this system.
Do complete the physical loop on every interactive surface: raised, lifted on hover, inset on press.
Do put uppercase labels at 600 weight with 0.1em tracking, never less.
Do show 'unknown' rather than a reassuring default when data is missing — the 'Allergens Unknown' chip is the reference implementation.
Do re-tint --neu-shadow-dark / --neu-shadow-light when placing neumorphic surfaces on a non-standard ground, as .neu-scope-navy does.
Do cap layouts at max-w-md and design for one hand.
Do disable looping motion under prefers-reduced-motion while keeping the static depth, which is styling rather than movement.
donts: Don't introduce a decorative accent colour. If it isn't reporting a reading, it doesn't get colour.
Don't put a border on the outer edge of a raised surface — the shadow pair is that edge.

Don't use a generic single drop shadow (0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.1)) on a surface that sits on the instrument body. It reads as a foreign object. The legacy .sleek-shadow helper predates this system; prefer neu-raised.
Don't light anything from a direction other than top-left.
Don't build a full-bleed opaque panel as a dialog. Dialogs are centred 24px-radius cards over a dimmed, blurred backdrop; a full-screen takeover reads as the page breaking.
Don't animate width, height, top or left. Transform and opacity only.
Don't add a tablet or desktop layout without an explicit decision — the fixed phone frame is intentional.
